Solution: Use the addition rule with the given intersection: 1/2+3/10-1/10=7/10. The overlap is included once, not removed entirely.

Question Choices: For mutually exclusive events with P(A)=0.2 and P(B)=0.35 find P(A or B).
Hints: Mutually exclusive events have no overlap.;Add the probabilities.
Solution: The intersection is zero because the events are mutually exclusive. Hence P(A or B)=P(A)+P(B)=1/5+7/20=11/20. The result lies between 0 and 1.

Question Choices: If P(A or B)=0.9 P(A)=0.6 and P(B)=0.5 find P(A and B).
Hints: Rearrange the addition rule.;P(A and B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A or B).
Solution: Rearrange P(A or B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A and B) to isolate the overlap. P(A and B)=3/5+1/2-9/10=1/5. Check that the overlap is nonnegative and no larger than either event probability.

Question Choices: A standard deck has 4 kings and 13 spades with one king of spades. One card is drawn uniformly from all 52 cards. Find P(king or spade).
Solution: The rank contributes 4 cards and the suit 13, including one shared card. Subtract that overlap once: (4+13-1)/52=16/52=4/13. All 52 cards are equally likely under the stated uniform draw.

Question Choices: A Venn diagram has 10 in A only 6 in B only 4 in both and 20 outside. How many outcomes are in the sample space?
Solution: The four regions are disjoint and exhaustive, so add each once: 10+6+4+20=40 outcomes. The outside region is part of the sample space too.
